plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: Enormous, fragrant, bowl-shaped blooms unfurl from plump round buds, with layers of silky petals that ripple like ruffled satin. Gardens fill with a sweet, rosy perfume, and the flowers often grow heavy enough to bow their stems.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer, peaking from mid-May to mid-June in temperate Northern Hemisphere gardens
plants.location: Temperate gardens of North America, Europe and East Asia, with native roots in northern China and Siberia
plants.funFact: Peonies can live and bloom for more than 50 years in the same spot, and they have been cultivated in China for well over a thousand years.

plants.name: Rosa gallica
plants.description: One of the oldest garden roses, it bears richly scented, semi-double flowers in deep crimson and pink, each with a golden heart of stamens. Its upright, thorny shrubs often form dense thickets that blaze with color.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late May through June, with a single main flush in late spring to early summer
plants.location: Central and southern Europe and western Asia, widely grown in gardens across the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Its petals keep their fragrance even when dried, so medieval apothecaries used it for perfumes, medicines and potpourri.

plants.name: Camissonia cheiranthifolia
plants.description: A low, silvery mat of foliage hugs the coastal dunes, dotted with cheerful yellow blooms that open to catch the sea breeze. It is tough, salt-tolerant and perfectly suited to shifting sand.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring through late summer, roughly April to August
plants.location: Coastal dunes and beaches of California and Oregon, USA, and Baja California, Mexico
plants.funFact: Its silvery, hairy leaves reflect harsh sunlight and trap moisture, which helps it survive in salty, windswept sand.
